chunks: And the heavens, how it was raised high;
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran describe the raising of the heavens in Surah Al-Ghashiyah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited alongside the subsequent command to 'look at the camels' to illustrate the progression from macrocosmic signs (the heavens) to microcosmic ones (creation), inviting rational contemplation (aql). It underscores the ease (Yusr) of Allah's creative act, contrasting the vastness of the sky with the humility required of the observer, a theme central to the Surah's call to reflection before the Day of Judgment.
